blocks.heading: Is Gildan Activewear’s dividend covered by its cash?

paragraphs.text: Free cash flow is the money left after operating the business and buying necessary long-lived assets. In 2024, Gildan generated US$340,812 thousand but paid US$889,077 thousand in dividends and buybacks, creating a US$548,265 thousand shortfall. New debt of US$800,000 thousand helped cover that gap, while repayments totalled US$235,000 thousand. Shareholders received cash, but borrowing supplied part of it.

By 2025, free cash flow covered dividends and buybacks, leaving US$152,592 thousand before acquisitions and other uses. Yet net debt rose to US$4,029,222 thousand from US$1,437,071 thousand in 2024. Gildan let its buyback authorization expire on August 8, 2025, and said repurchases would wait until leverage returned toward its target range.

blocks.heading: What has Gildan Activewear guided for 2026?

paragraphs.text: Management’s promise is to earn more from each sales dollar in 2026, not simply to sell more garments. It guides to US$6,000 million of revenue and a 21.8% adjusted operating margin. Adjusted diluted earnings per share are guided to US$4.65–US$4.75, representing growth of 32.5%–35.0%. An operating margin is the share of sales left after manufacturing and operating costs.

Tariff refunds and integration savings support the forecast. Gildan expects US$220 million of IEEPA refunds in 2026 and US$100 million of targeted integration savings. Refunds are largely nonrecurring, while qualifying Central American production can receive continuing tariff relief; management plans to reinvest much of the temporary benefit in brands, products and packaging.

Those milestones are encouraging, but an implemented initiative and a full year of realized savings are not the same thing.

blocks.heading: What were Gildan Activewear's last eight quarters of results?

paragraphs.text: Revenue grew 72.3% year over year because the comparison was Gildan alone against the combined Gildan–Hanes business. Against a comparable combined-business base, sales declined 7.9%. Earlier customer pre-buying and current channel inventory reductions explain part of the difference, but retail demand and seasonal stocking were also softer.

Operating cash flow reached 347,436 in June, but first-half free cash flow remained negative 28,718. The quarter therefore combines recovery, seasonality, acquisition effects and unusual income. The next question is whether customers are replenishing their stocks.

L’amortissement comptabilise l’utilisation graduelle d’un actif incorporel acquis. Gildan en a comptabilisé 29 millions $ US au premier semestre de 2026, principalement pour les relations avec les clients de Hanes. Il ne s’agit pas d’un nouveau paiement effectué au cours de cette période, mais ces relations doivent tout de même conserver leur valeur.

blocks.heading: Quelles prévisions Gildan Activewear a-t-elle fournies pour 2026?

paragraphs.text: La promesse de la direction est de tirer davantage de chaque dollar de ventes en 2026, et non simplement de vendre plus de vêtements. Elle prévoit des produits de 6 000 millions $ US et une marge d’exploitation ajustée de 21,8 %. Le bénéfice ajusté dilué par action prévu s’établit entre 4,65 $ US et 4,75 $ US, ce qui représente une croissance de 32,5 % à 35,0 %. La marge d’exploitation correspond à la part des ventes qui reste après les coûts de fabrication et d’exploitation.

Les remboursements de droits de douane et les économies liées à l’intégration soutiennent les prévisions. Gildan prévoit recevoir 220 millions $ US de remboursements au titre de l’IEEPA en 2026 et réaliser 100 millions $ US d’économies d’intégration ciblées. Les remboursements sont en grande partie non récurrents, tandis que la production admissible en Amérique centrale peut bénéficier d’un allègement tarifaire continu; la direction prévoit réinvestir une grande partie de l’avantage temporaire dans les marques, les produits et l’emballage.
